newsitem.title: POLAND: Rains continue over Poland bracing for new floods.
newsitem.headline: Rains continue over Poland bracing for new floods.

text.p: Rain continued over most of Poland through the night but its lower intensity and better flood defences meant a new catastrophe should be avoided, the central crisis committee's spokesman said on Sunday.

"It's raining everywhere -- not the very intensive rainfalls that had been expected but a flood threat still exists," spokesman Krzysztof Pomes told Reuters, adding that forecasts showed more rain for Sunday and Monday.
"For the time being it's bad but there's no tragedy as far as the rainfall is concerned," Pomes said, adding that rain was expected to continue into Monday.

He said constant rain continued in parts of Poland's southwest such as the town of Legnica, but the army, fire brigades and ordinary citizens were building barriers and repairing damaged dykes against the new onslaught.

"Everywhere in Legnica they're battling and the water is lowering...they're on flood alert but not to the degree that it has spilled over the protective barriers. The lesson from the previous phase is that all are working to prevent another tragedy," Pomes said.

The new rain starting on Thursday night has struck a Poland just deciding how best to rebuild after floods over the past two weeks killed 49 people, inundated a thousand towns and villages and swamped 5,000 sq km in the south and west.
